normal_outcome_power_check.verdict: textbook formula validated: power near 0.80 when its normality assumption holds

overall: Investigation of the 6.2% null rate found TWO real issues, both fixed. (1) A bug in the OBF boundary recursion: the survival truncation was applied after propagation instead of before, making later bounds too liberal (family-wise error 0.060 under the canonical model). Fixed; the Brownian check now gives 0.0506 with CI [0.0496, 0.0516] and per-look increments matching the spending function. (2) A flawed validation design: the first bootstrap kept hash-fixed arms, freezing each seed's realized finite-population difference, which the test then rightly rejected more often at larger n/N. Replaced with a permutation null (exchangeable arms): about 0.05 at both sizes on real outcomes. The textbook formula is validated (power 0.80 at 482/arm on normal data). The replay power shortfall is fully explained by the 5-star ceiling, corrected by the calibrated size of about 750/arm.
